summary: NEW ACTIONABLE CANDIDATE: Rico Dowdle Over 8.5 rushing attempts. Dimers' publicly timestamped board was last updated 2026-09-18 01:08 ET and showed FanDuel O8.5 -114; ScoresAndOdds' current Week 2 page also exposes an O8.5 -115 quote in its bet365 column, while its consensus rush-attempt market is 9.5 O-122/U-108. The isolated 8.5 is materially better than consensus. This is not projection-only: FantasyPros' Week 2 role analysis says Dowdle started Week 1, led Pittsburgh RBs with 57.8% snaps, 48.8% route share and the only red-zone carry, even though Jaylen Warren out-carried him 10-8. The backfield remains a committee and Pittsburgh is a 4.5-point road underdog, so PRIME discounts the more aggressive external projections and assigns a conservative 61% fair Over probability at 8.5. At -114/-115 that produces about a 7.5-7.7 percentage-point raw edge. Recommendation: 0.5u BET_NOW only if the live regulated sportsbook still shows 8.5 at -115 or better. Do not chase 9.5 at the current consensus -122 and do not pay worse than -115 at 8.5. Bucky Irving receiving and rush attempts remain WATCH/REDUCED_EDGE; Quinshon Judkins attempts remains PASS_AFTER_MOVE. No new Grok pass.

decisions.reason: The 8.5 threshold is materially below both the current ScoresAndOdds consensus market of 9.5 and multiple independent workload estimates. Week 1 role evidence supports Dowdle remaining part of a true two-back committee: he started, led RB snaps 57.8%-35.9%, led route share 48.8%-30.2%, and handled Pittsburgh's only RB red-zone carry, though Warren had 10 carries to Dowdle's 8 and was more efficient. FantasyPros explicitly notes the role/workload signals conflict and treats the matchup as favorable. Dynasty Spec projects 12.2 carries; ScoresAndOdds projects 10.3; Dimers' model is much more aggressive at roughly 82% Over probability. PRIME does not adopt that 82% estimate. It uses a conservative 61% fair probability to account for Warren's better Week 1 efficiency, the committee structure, Pittsburgh being a road underdog, and LT Troy Fautanu being limited with an ankle injury. At the isolated 8.5/-114 to -115 price, the edge still clears PRIME's threshold. At consensus 9.5/-122, it does not.

No new overnight information resolves the projection disagreement recorded at 02:14 ET. Sean Tucker remains on track to return after full practices Wednesday and Thursday. Do not restore the prior BET_NOW state without a stronger price or materially new role information.
Remains a WATCH because current models disagree materially and Sean Tucker is expected back. Friday final designations remain a required checkpoint.

No fresh sportsbook-specific O12.5 at -110 or better was verified. Cleveland's Thursday injury report still has Teven Jenkins DNP and Parker Brailsford/Elgton Jenkins limited, so no new offensive-line catalyst justifies chasing higher attempt thresholds.
